\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رنجش} (ranjish)}{رنجش (ranjish)}]{\ur{رنجش} (ranjish) — ill feeling; a grudge}

\label{lesson:UR-C491-ranjish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an orphan, then the Urdu for to adopt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رنجش}}
\textbf{\ur{رنجش}} — \emph{ranjish} — \textquotedblleft{}ill feeling; a grudge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دونوں} \ur{بھائیوں} \ur{میں} \ur{رنجش} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{donoṅ bhāiyoṅ meṅ ranjish hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is ill feeling between the two brothers.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رنجش}} (\emph{ranjish}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{ranjish}, \textquotedblleft{}offence, vexation\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ranjish}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ranjish}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{donoṅ bhāiyoṅ meṅ ranjish hai.} — There is ill feeling between the two brothers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an orphan, then the Urdu for to adopt, then say \emph{ranjish} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{رنجش} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Ill feeling; a grudge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شکوہ} (shikvā)}{شکوہ (shikvā)}]{\ur{شکوہ} (shikvā) — a grievance; a complaint (to someone close)}

\label{lesson:UR-C491-shikva}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to adopt, then the Urdu for ill feeling.

\textbf{\ur{شکوہ}} — \emph{shikvā} — \textquotedblleft{}a grievance; a complaint (to someone close)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{use apne dost se shikvā hai.}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{طعنہ} (tānā)}{طعنہ (tānā)}]{\ur{طعنہ} (tānā) — a taunt}

\label{lesson:UR-C491-tana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for ill feeling, then the Urdu for a grievance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{طعنہ}}
\textbf{\ur{طعنہ}} — \emph{tānā} — \textquotedblleft{}a taunt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بھائی} \ur{نے} \ur{دیر} \ur{سے} \ur{آنے} \ur{پر} \ur{طعنہ} \ur{دیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhāī ne der se āne par tānā diyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother made a dig about my coming late.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{طعنہ}} (\emph{tānā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ṭaʿna}, \textquotedblleft{}a thrust\textquotedblright{}, and so a cutting remark.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{معاف} \ur{کرنا} (māf karnā)}{معاف کرنا (māf karnā)}]{\ur{معاف} \ur{کرنا} (māf karnā) — to forgive}

\label{lesson:UR-C491-maf-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a taunt, then the Urdu for a divorce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{معاف} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{معاف} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{māf karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to forgive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بہن} \ur{نے} \ur{بھائی} \ur{کو} \ur{معاف} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bahan ne bhāī ko māf kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sister forgave her brother.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{دوست} \ur{کو} \ur{معاف} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne dost ko māf kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{معاف} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{māf karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{معاف}}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muʿāf}, \textquotedblleft{}excused\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māf karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māf karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahan ne bhāī ko māf kiyā.} — The sister forgave her brother.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a taunt, then the Urdu for a divorce, then say \emph{māf karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{معاف} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To forgive\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
